$$A=1_p\otimes W_m\otimes1_n:t\longrightarrow r+s,\qquad B=1_p\otimes B_m\otimes1_n:r+s\longrightarrow t,$$
$$\alpha=(p_r\otimes p_s)Ap_t,\qquad \beta=p_tB(p_r\otimes p_s),\qquad \Theta(m,n,p)=\operatorname{Tr}_t(\beta\alpha).$$

This fixes the vertex without a further scalar normalization. The theta net has the three JW-labelled edges $r,s,t$, since idempotence collapses the doubled projectors. Its value is
$$\Theta(m,n,p)=\frac{[m]![n]![p]![h+1]!}{[m+n]![n+p]![m+p]!}.$$

$$[m+p][n+p]\Theta(m,n,p)=[p][m+n+p+1]\Theta(m,n,p-1),\qquad \Theta(m,n,0)=[m+n+1].$$

More explicitly, choose the normalized path matrix units $F_{p,q}$ whose prefix inclusions satisfy $F_{p,q}\mapsto\sum_c F_{pc,qc}$. If $pc,qc$ end at $c$, with predecessor endpoints $a,b$, then
$$\bar E_n(F_{pc,qc})=\begin{cases}\dfrac{[c+1]}{\delta[a+1]}F_{p,q},&a=b,\\0,&a\ne b.\end{cases}$$
Here the extensions and matrix units exist only for valid adjacent retained labels. The diagonal trace is $\tau_n(F_{p,p})=\delta^{-n}[a+1]$ when $p$ ends at $a$. These assertions hold at every finite rank, including the $\ell=3$ boundary; no extra quotient/path identification is assumed.

affected_proof_uses: 1.1 The quantum-integer recurrence with real $\delta$ makes each $[r]$ real, and [F5] gives $[r]>0$ for $1\le r<\ell$. Starting with $p_0=p_1=1$, induction in the JW recursion shows $p_r^*=p_r$ through $r=\ell-1$: reflection fixes $P_r=p_r\otimes1$ and $U_r$, while the coefficient $[r]/[r+1]$ is real whenever this recursion is used. In particular the boundary projector $p_{\ell-1}$ is self-adjoint. For $n<\ell-1$, the generated ideal component $I_n$ is zero and is reflection-stable; for $n\ge\ell-1$, its fixed embedded generator $p_{\ell-1}\otimes1$ is self-adjoint, so $I_n=\mathrm{TL}_n(p_{\ell-1}\otimes1)\mathrm{TL}_n$ is reflection-stable because $(x(p_{\ell-1}\otimes1)y)^*=y^*(p_{\ell-1}\otimes1)x^*$. By [F3], these are the endomorphism components of the generated negligible tensor ideal. Also [F7] gives $\tau_n(D^*)=\overline{\tau_n(D)}$ on diagrams and hence on all elements. If $x\in J_n$, then for every $y$ cyclicity yields $\tau_n(yx^*)=\overline{\tau_n(xy^*)}=\overline{\tau_n(y^*x)}=0$; thus the trace radical is reflection-stable as well. Since [F3] identifies it with $I_n$, the quotient involution is well defined. [F2, F3, F5, F7, given, algebra]

1.2 Fix a retained endpoint $1\le a\le k$, write $f_a=p_a\otimes1$, and use the supplier's maps $\alpha_a=f_a(1_{a-1}\otimes\mathrm{cup})p_{a-1}$ and $\beta_a=p_{a-1}(1_{a-1}\otimes\mathrm{cap})f_a$. Horizontal reflection reverses composition and exchanges the cup and cap; step 1.1 fixes $f_a$ and $p_{a-1}$, so $\alpha_a^*=\beta_a$. The supplier identity $\beta_a\alpha_a=\lambda_a p_{a-1}$ therefore gives $\alpha_a^*\alpha_a=\lambda_a p_{a-1}$. Set $v_a=\lambda_a^{-1/2}\alpha_a$. Then $v_a^*v_a=p_{a-1}$ and $v_av_a^*=\lambda_a^{-1}\alpha_a\beta_a$, the down projection in the JW split. For $a<k$, the complementary up projection is $p_{a+1}$; it is self-adjoint by step 1.1 and orthogonal to the down projection by the JW turnback relations in [F2]. At $a=k$, the quotient kills $p_{k+1}=p_{\ell-1}$ before normalization, so only the down projection remains. The up inclusion and retraction are adjoints, as are $v_a$ and $v_a^*$. Composing these isometric branch maps along retained paths gives path maps $I_p$ with mutually orthogonal ranges and $\sum_p I_pI_p^*=1_n$. Hence $F_{p,q}=I_pI_q^*$ are complete matrix units and $F_{p,q}^*=F_{q,p}$. Their diagonal units equal the supplier's path projections (the reciprocal branch normalizations cancel), so $\operatorname{Tr}_n(F_{p,q})=\delta_{p,q}[a+1]$ by [F2]. Thus the quotient with its inherited reflection is a direct sum of full complex matrix algebras with the usual adjoint, hence a finite-dimensional $C^*$-algebra. Since $\tau_n(F_{p,p})=\delta^{-n}[a+1]>0$, its normalized closure trace is faithful positive. [F2, F3, F5, step 1.1, construct, algebra]

2.1 Tensoring an endpoint path map with a strand and resolving its endpoint identity by the same isometric up/down splitting gives $F_{p,q}\otimes1=\sum_c F_{pc,qc}$. The coefficients are exactly one because the inclusion and retraction at each common endpoint use reciprocal normalizations. At $a=k$ delete $p_{k+1}$ before splitting; only its down term remains, as in [F2]. Thus the actual quotient inclusions are exactly the prefix maps of [F4]; no compatibility is imposed as an additional hypothesis. Transporting the endpoint action along these matrix units and applying [F4] gives the asserted multiplicity-one branching, omitting zero path spaces and invalid boundary labels.
